_meta.version: MediGemma Field — ICD-11 Primary Care curated subset (2026-05)
_meta.description: Hand-curated subset of WHO ICD-11 entries most relevant to primary care triage in resource-limited settings. Selected to align with WHO ETAT emergency triage and WHO IMCI childhood illness protocols, plus tropical infectious diseases relevant to the target user population (Sub-Saharan Africa, refugee camps, conflict zones).
_meta.source: International Classification of Diseases, Eleventh Revision (ICD-11), World Health Organization (WHO) 2019/2021. https://icd.who.int/browse11
_meta.license: CC BY-ND 3.0 IGO. Data is reproduced without modification. Codes and titles are quoted verbatim from ICD-11. The canonical linearization URI for each entry is constructed at runtime as 'https://id.who.int/icd/release/11/mms/{code}' and included in every grounded prompt, satisfying the ICD-11 software-license requirement to preserve codes and URIs (ICD-11 Reference Guide §0.1). Keyword tags and primary_care_note fields are MediGemma Field annotations and are clearly identified as additions that do not originate from WHO (permitted under §0.1).
_meta.disclaimer: This subset is not an authoritative diagnostic dataset. It is a triage-aid lookup to ground LLM outputs in standard medical taxonomy. Always verify against official ICD-11 references for clinical use.

entries.title: Cholera
entries.primary_care_note: Severe acute watery diarrhea with rapid dehydration. Level 3 if shock or extreme dehydration. Oral rehydration urgent.

entries.title: Typhoid fever
entries.primary_care_note: Sustained high fever with GI symptoms in endemic areas. Antibiotic treatment required.

entries.title: Malaria
entries.primary_care_note: Fever with chills/rigors in endemic area. P. falciparum can be Level 3 (cerebral malaria). Test and treat urgently.

entries.title: Dengue fever
entries.primary_care_note: High fever with severe muscle/joint pain in endemic area. Watch for warning signs (bleeding, abdominal pain) → Level 3.

entries.title: Pneumonia
entries.primary_care_note: Fever + productive cough + breathing difficulty. WHO IMCI: rapid breathing in children = Level 3 (severe pneumonia).

entries.title: Acute upper respiratory infection
entries.primary_care_note: Self-limiting. Home care with rest and fluids. Watch for worsening → escalate.

entries.title: Acute bronchitis
entries.primary_care_note: Cough lasting 1-3 weeks after URI. Antibiotics usually not needed unless bacterial superinfection.

entries.title: Acute bronchiolitis (RSV)
entries.primary_care_note: Children under 2: rapid breathing or chest indrawing = Level 3 per WHO IMCI.

entries.title: Acute pharyngitis
entries.primary_care_note: Most viral. Strep (bacterial) needs antibiotics if confirmed.

entries.title: Asthma exacerbation
entries.primary_care_note: Inability to speak in full sentences = Level 3. Bronchodilator inhaler urgent.

entries.title: Acute coronary syndrome
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. Time-critical. Activate emergency services immediately.

entries.title: Stroke (cerebrovascular accident)
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. FAST signs (Face/Arm/Speech/Time) = transport immediately. Time window critical.

entries.title: Convulsions / seizures
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3 if first seizure or status epilepticus (>5 min). WHO ETAT priority sign.

entries.title: Meningitis
entries.primary_care_note: Fever + stiff neck = Level 3. Time-critical antibiotic treatment.

entries.title: Acute appendicitis
entries.primary_care_note: Classic migration of pain from periumbilical to RLQ. Surgical emergency.

entries.title: Acute gastroenteritis
entries.primary_care_note: Most self-limiting. Level 3 if signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, no urine, lethargy).

entries.title: Peptic ulcer disease
entries.primary_care_note: Burning epigastric pain. Black stools (melena) or hematemesis = Level 3 (GI bleed).

entries.title: Ectopic pregnancy
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. Reproductive-age woman with abdominal pain + missed period must rule this out. Surgical emergency.

entries.title: Threatened or spontaneous miscarriage
entries.primary_care_note: Bleeding in pregnancy. Heavy bleeding or shock signs = Level 3.

entries.title: Pre-eclampsia / eclampsia
entries.primary_care_note: Pregnancy >20 weeks + headache/swelling/vision changes = Level 3.

entries.title: Acute pyelonephritis (kidney infection)
entries.primary_care_note: Fever + flank pain + UTI symptoms. Antibiotics urgent. Sepsis signs = Level 3.

entries.title: Lower urinary tract infection (cystitis)
entries.primary_care_note: Uncomplicated UTI. Treat with antibiotics. Level 1 unless fever or back pain.

entries.title: Tuberculosis (pulmonary)
entries.primary_care_note: Cough >2 weeks + weight loss + night sweats. Sputum test essential. Coughing blood = Level 3.

entries.title: HIV / AIDS
entries.primary_care_note: Specialist referral. Acute opportunistic infections (PCP, cryptococcal meningitis) = Level 3.

entries.title: Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. Diabetic with vomiting + rapid breathing + altered consciousness.

entries.title: Hypoglycemia
entries.primary_care_note: Diabetic + confusion/altered consciousness = Level 3. Give sugar immediately if able to swallow.

entries.title: Cellulitis
entries.primary_care_note: Antibiotics needed. Spreading rapidly, fever, or near eye/face = Level 3.

entries.title: Burns
entries.primary_care_note: Level depends on size and depth. >10% body surface, face, hands, or genitals = Level 3.

entries.title: Head injury / concussion
entries.primary_care_note: LOC, vomiting, severe headache, or worsening over hours = Level 3 (intracranial hemorrhage).

entries.title: Snake bite
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. Immobilize limb, transport to facility with antivenom. Do not cut/suck wound.

entries.title: Severe dehydration
entries.primary_care_note: WHO ETAT priority sign. Especially critical in children. IV or NG fluids needed.

entries.title: Acute conjunctivitis
entries.primary_care_note: Self-limiting if viral. Topical antibiotics if bacterial. Pain/vision loss = Level 3 (rule out keratitis/uveitis).

entries.title: Acute otitis media
entries.primary_care_note: Common in children. Antibiotics if severe or prolonged. Mastoiditis (swelling behind ear) = Level 3.

entries.title: Lower back pain (non-specific)
entries.primary_care_note: Most self-limiting. Red flags: trauma, fever, weakness, bowel/bladder dysfunction → Level 3 (cauda equina).

entries.title: Vaginal bleeding (abnormal uterine)
entries.primary_care_note: Reproductive age + heavy bleeding + lightheaded = consider Level 3 (hemorrhage).

entries.title: Anaphylaxis
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. Epinephrine immediately if available. Airway compromise risk.

entries.title: Eczema / atopic dermatitis
entries.primary_care_note: Chronic. Topical emollients and steroids. Infection (oozing, crusting) = treat.

entries.title: Scabies
entries.primary_care_note: Common in crowded settings (refugee camps). Permethrin treatment. Treat all close contacts.

entries.title: Acute malnutrition (severe)
entries.primary_care_note: WHO IMCI: bilateral edema or MUAC <115mm in children = Level 3. Therapeutic feeding required.

entries.title: Sepsis
entries.primary_care_note: Always Level 3. WHO ETAT priority sign. Time-critical antibiotic + fluid resuscitation.
